question: A teacher was leading a class of four perfectly logical students. The teacher chose a set $S$ of four integers and gave a different number in $S$ to each student. Then the teacher announced to the class that the numbers in $S$ were four consecutive two-digit positive integers, that some number in $S$ was divisible by $6$ , and a different number in $S$ was divisible by $7$ . The teacher then asked if any of the students could deduce what $S$ is, but in unison, all of the students replied no. However, upon hearing that all four students replied no, each student was able to determine the elements of $S$ . Find the sum of all possible values of the greatest element of $S$ .

The teacher told them that in S, there's a number divisible by 6 and a different number divisible by 7. When asked if anyone could deduce S, all said no. But upon hearing that everyone said no, they all figured out S. We need to find the sum of all possible values of the greatest element of S.

Also, among these four numbers, one is divisible by 6, another is divisible by 7, and they are different numbers. So, in S, there's a multiple of 6 and a multiple of 7, which are distinct.

So, the fact that no one could deduce S initially gives them additional information, allowing them to eliminate possibilities and find S uniquely.
